resumen: Sitting on a bench reclined backwards, with the arms hanging behind the torso, you curl the dumbbells up. The shoulder stays back and the biceps works in a stretched position.
ejecucion: Set the back rest to about 45-60° and sit with your back supported and a dumbbell in each hand.
Let your straight arms hang towards the floor, behind the line of your torso, palms facing forward.
Curl the dumbbells up by bending your elbows, without letting the elbows move forward.
Lower slowly until your arms are fully straight.
If you feel a pull at the front of your shoulder, raise the back rest so the arm sits less far back.
matices: In a study of twenty-two people comparing the standing, incline and preacher curls, the incline and standing curls activated the biceps similarly throughout the range, while the preacher curl did so only over a short stretch. What changes is the position, not the measured activation: with the shoulder behind the torso, the biceps works in a more stretched position. Whether that adds anything was not measured in this study.

fuentes.titulo: Effect of the shoulder position on the biceps brachii EMG in different dumbbell curls
fuentes.autor: Oliveira et al., J Sports Sci Med, 2009

fuentes.titulo: Essentials of Strength Training and Conditioning (4th ed.)
